messages:
omar: Quick follow-up from the offload/paging RFC — I sketched a small set of interface proposals and tradeoffs. want feedback on APIs + operational story before we lock the design.

omar: Problem restated: we need predictable latency for hot requests while enabling large-model working sets via GPU->CPU offload. main concerns: fragmentation, eviction latency, correctness across streams, and observability.

elaine: high level 👍. quick thought: split allocator responsibilities — a tiny fast bump-pointer for ephemeral per-request allocations + a pooled allocator for long-lived KV/cache tensors. fragmentation mostly hits pooled area.

zack: agree. also: add 'pinned' vs 'pageable' semantics to the contract. pinned = cannot be evicted, pageable = candidate for async offload. makes scheduler simpler.

sue: calling out CUDA UM (unified memory) — it hides paging but hooks into driver-managed migration. pros: fewer code paths. cons: unpredictable page faults and cross-device stalls. i'd avoid relying on UM for tail-latency SLOs.

omar: +1 on pinned/pageable. proposal: public allocator API:

```
allocate_gpu(size, mode="ephemeral"|"pinned"|"pageable") -> handle
async_offload(handle) -> future
async_prefetch(handle) -> future
pin(handle) / unpin(handle)
query_fragmentation() -> {percent, largest_free}
```

omar: Questions: 1) should offload be synchronous from user thread or always async? 2) should we expose eviction heuristics to apps, or keep heuristics internal with telemetry knobs?

elaine: 1) async only. sync offload will block decode/inference path and cause head-of-line problems. expose a small sync_wait(handle, timeout) only for debugging.

zack: 2) keep heuristics internal but pluggable. think default LRU-ish policy tuned for tensor lifetimes + usage score. provide hooks: serve_eviction_score(handle) and a callback interface for advanced users.

sue: we need a compact-on-demand API. when fragmentation > X% we should be able to compact background or during low load. compaction must be cooperative with CUDA streams. also record compaction cost to metrics.

omar: compaction + cooperative streams — noted. how do we measure fragmentation accurately? per-GPU free-list snapshots? running a best-fit scan is expensive.

elaine: maintain lightweight coarse bins + background defrag. bins track free extents by size class; fragmentation = 1 - (sum_largest_bin_free / total_free). approximates worst-case packing.

zack: also export a small synthetic benchmark:

```
# run on a node under load to estimate offload cost
python perf/offload_bench.py --gpu 0 --alloc-pattern=chatty --working-set=60GB
```

zack: results should feed into Optimize suggestions (batch sizes, preferred quantization) later.

omar: operational story: feature-flagged rollout, start with pageable disabled by default. enable in canary pool with telemetry for evictions, offload latency (p90/p99), remote PCIe stalls.

infra-bot: ci:offload-rfc-tests — 3/12 flaky tests; link: https://ci.internal/123/offload-rfc-tests

elaine: can we add deterministic tests for eviction ordering? e.g., synthetic lifetimes + a fake clock to assert which pages get evicted. helps avoid racy bugs.

omar: yes — add a "test-mode" allocator that exposes eviction sequence and bypasses async. good to catch edge cases.

sue: cross-node memory: if we ever do GPU pooling across nodes, offload targets expand to remote node CPU memory — need network-aware eviction policy (don't evict to remote unless cheap). out of scope for initial MVP but we should design interfaces accordingly.

omar: good call. keep OffloadTarget abstraction so we can add local-CPU, host-pinned, NVMe, remote-CPU later.

zack: tiny nit: add backpressure signals to upstream: if background offload backlog > threshold, reject or shed low-priority requests. otherwise queue grows and p99 explodes.

omar: agreed. add metrics: offload_queue_len, avg_offload_ms, compaction_ms, fragmentation_pct, eviction_count, bytes_moved. these feed Console dashboards and Optimize hints.

elaine: doc action items: i'll write a follow-up that maps the API + lifecycle diagram (alloc -> use -> async_offload -> evict -> reclaim -> compact). will include sequence diagrams.

omar: thanks — i'll add a small RFC appendix with canary rollout plan and test checklist. let's aim to merge the initial allocator patch behind a feature flag by EOW.

zack: :thumbsup:

sue: :thinking: one more — consider GPU memory coloring / tagging to track which subsystem owns blocks (chat vs caching) so compaction/eviction policies can be weighted. helps prevent noisy neighbors.

omar: nice idea. include tag labels in handle metadata. ok that's all for now, thanks everyone.
